hook_text: Every flowering plant in your garden is on one of two teams. Split a bean and you will see why.
clip_script: Soak a bean and a mealie grain overnight. The bean splits into two fat halves: two seed leaves. Team Two, the dicots. The mealie will not split: one seed leaf and a big store of starch, the part that becomes mealie meal. Team One, the monocots. Now check the grown plants. Hold a leaf to the light. Train-track veins? Team One. A branching net? Team Two. Pull up the roots. A beard of thin roots? Team One. One main root, like a carrot? Team Two. Count the petals. Threes or sixes? Team One. Fours or fives? Team Two. Grass, mealies and aloes: Team One. Beans, proteas and the baobab: Team Two.
visual_style: Whiteboard bean splitting open next to an unsplittable mealie grain; split-screen leaf, root and flower comparisons with big ONE and TWO badges.
pacing: Quick seed split, three rapid checks, a fast team roll-call.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort every plant in your garden into a team.
